newsitem.title: USA: US West in largest-ever investment-grade bond issue.
newsitem.headline: US West in largest-ever investment-grade bond issue.

text.p: Regional telephone company U.S. West Inc. sold $4.1 billion in corporate bonds Thursday, setting a record for the largest investment-grade debt offering ever in the United States.
The prior largest issue of investment-grade bonds was Lockheed Martin Corp.'s $3.5 billion offering last year.

US West Treasurer James Anderson said the proceeds from the offering will be used by U.S. West to refinance debt incurred during its acquisition of Continental Cablevision Inc. of Boston, Mass., last year.
The offering was underwritten by a syndicate of investment banks led by Merrill Lynch & Co.
Traders and analysts noted the offering was increased in size to $4.1 billion from $2 billion as a result of strong demand by Wall Street investors.
The bonds, issued by a finance subsidiary of U.S. West, ranged in maturities from five- to 100 years.
U.S. West, based in Englewood, Colo., is the holding company for U.S. West Communications Group, a local telephone company, and U.S. West Media Group, a cable TV and media company.
Investment-grade bonds are "high-quality" bonds issued by corporations with strong balance sheets. High yield or "junk" bonds are considered more speculative investments.
The only other deal of comparable size to the US West issue was the $4.1 billion "junk bond" offering by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp in 1989.
